correctness.rationale: The radial projection has arc-length Jacobian <x,nu>/|x|^2 on the regular boundary, giving positive weight |x|^2<x,nu>/2 with the declared normalization. The support assumption puts arc-length almost every boundary point in the four closed supporting faces. Their relative complement, if nonempty, would contain a nonzero-length open boundary arc, so the entire boundary lies in those faces and the body equals the coordinate rectangle. Integrating b(b^2+y^2)/2 on the right facet gives b^3(c+d)/2+b(c^3+d^3)/6, and reflection/interchange gives the other masses. Strict monotonicity in the horizontal half-width forces equality of the two half-widths. After writing d=as, c=ast, lambda=(3+kappa)/(2+6kappa) fixes exactly one positive kappa iff 1/6<lambda<3/2. The positive-denominator derivative numerator of F_kappa is -(1+3kappa)[(t^2-t+1)^2+9kappa t^2], and F_kappa ranges from infinity to zero. Thus beta fixes a unique t (not 1 when B!=C); s and the positive scale follow, with all masses recovered. Varying lambda across the open range at fixed nonunit beta gives sharpness even at fixed imbalance. The endpoint obstruction requires an origin-interior body.
